bull.b: Statistically significant interim efficacy across skin and itch measures, with no treatment-related serious adverse events, strengthens QRX003’s development prospects. In a disease with no approved therapy, this could support future regulatory progress and commercial adoption.

Multiple rare-disease designations can provide regulatory interaction, review benefits and potential market exclusivity. These advantages may reduce development friction and strengthen QRX003’s strategic position if clinical efficacy is confirmed.

The planned financing supports clinical development over several years and reduces near-term dependence on additional raises. A longer runway gives Quoin more time to advance QRX003 toward pivotal data and potential commercialization milestones.

bear.b: Absence of revenue confirms that Quoin remains dependent on financing rather than commercial cash inflows. Until a product is approved and launched, development spending will continue without a proven recurring revenue base.

Persistently negative and worsening free cash flow increases reliance on external capital to fund operations and trials. This can constrain strategic flexibility and create ongoing financing risk before any product generates cash.

Falling equity and assets reflect accumulated losses and ongoing resource consumption despite no reported debt. Further funding may be required, creating dilution risk and reducing the financial cushion available for clinical execution.
